A most grave exhortation, wherein which he showeth how that sacrifice of Christ may be applied to us: to wit, by faith, which also he describeth, by the consequence, to wit, by sanctification of the Spirit, which causeth us surely to hope in God, and to procure by all means possible one another’s salvation, through the love that is in us one toward another.
With no double and counterfeit heart, but with such an heart as is truly and indeed given to God.
58:10:23: With the grace of the holy Ghost.
58:10:25: Having mentioned the last coming of Christ, he stirreth up the godly to the meditation of an holy life, and cites the faithless fallers from God, to the fearful judgment seat of the judge, because they wickedly rejected him in whom only salvation consisteth.
58:10:26: Without any cause or occasion, or show of occasion.
58:10:27: For it is another matter to sin through the frailty of man’s nature, and another thing to proclaim war as it were to God as to an enemy.
58:10:28: If the breach of the Law of Moses was punished by death, how much more worthy death is it to fall away from Christ?
58:10:30: The reason of all these things is, because God is a revenger of such as despise him: otherwise he should not rightly govern his Church. Now there is nothing more horrible then the wrath of the living God.
58:10:32: As he terrified the fallers away from God so doth he now comfort them that are constant and stand strongly setting before them the success of their former fights, so stirring them up to a sure hope of a full and ready victory.
58:10:33: You were brought forth to be ashamed.
In taking their miseries, to be your miseries.
58:10:37: He will come within this very little while.
58:10:38: He commendeth the excellency of a sure faith by the effect, because it is the only way to life, which sentence he setteth forth and amplifieth by setting the contrary against it.
58:11:1: An excellent description of faith by the effects, because it representeth things which are but yet in hope, and setteth as it were before our eyes things that are invisible.
58:11:2: He showeth that the Fathers ought to be accounted of, by this virtue.
That is, those Fathers of whom we came: and whose authority and example ought to move us very much.
58:11:3: So that the world which we see, was not made of any matter that appeared or was before, but of nothing.
He showeth the propriety of faith, by setting unto us most piked examples of such as from the beginning of the world excelled in the Church.
58:11:6: This reward is not referred to our merits, but to the free promise, as Paul teacheth in Abraham the father of all the faithful, Rom. 4:4.
58:11:10: This foundation is set against their tabernacle.
58:11:12: As unlikely to bear children, as if she had been stark dead.
58:11:13: For the Patriarchs were wont when they received the promises, to profess their religion, by building of altars, and calling on the name of the Lord.
In faith, which they had while they lived, and followed them even to their grave.
This is the figure Metonymy, for the things promised.
58:11:17: Although the promises of life were made in that only begotten Son Isaac, yet he appointed him to die, and so against hope he believed in hope.
58:11:19: For there was not the true and very death of Isaac, but as it were the death, by means whereof he seemed also as it were to have risen again.
58:11:23: They were not afraid to bring him up.
58:11:25: Such pleasures as he could not enjoy, but he must needs provoke God’s wrath against him.
58:11:31: Courteously and friendly, so that she did not only not hurt them, but also kept them safe.
A notable example of God’s goodness.
58:11:32: Gideon, Barak and other Judges and Prophets.
58:11:35: He seemeth to mean the story of that woman of Zarephath, whose son Elijah raised again from death, and the Shunammite, whose son Elisha restored to his mother.
He meaneth that persecution which Antiochus wrought.
58:11:37: In vile and rough clothing, so were the saints brought to extreme poverty, and constrained to live like beasts in wildernesses.
58:11:39: An amplification taken of the circumstance of the time: their faith is so much the more to be marveled at, by how much the promises of things to come were more dark, yet at length were indeed exhibited to us, so that their faith and ours is as one, as is also their consecration and ours.
58:11:40: For their salvation did hang upon Christ, who was exhibited in our days.
58:12:1: For sin besiegeth us on all sides, so that we cannot escape out.
An applying of the former examples, whereby we ought to be stirred up to run the whole race, casting away all stops and impediments.
58:12:2: Whereas he had all kind of blessedness in his hand and power, yet suffered willingly the ignominy of the cross.
He setteth before us, as the mark of this race, Jesus himself our captain, who willingly overcame all the roughness of the same way.
As it were upon the mark of our faith.
58:12:3: An amplification taken of the circumstance of the person, and the things themselves, which he compareth betwixt themselves: for how great is Jesus in comparison of us, and how far more grievous things did he suffer than we?
58:12:4: He taketh an argument of the profit which cometh to us by God’s chastisements, unless we be in fault. First of all because sin, or that rebellious wickedness of our flesh, is by this means turned.
58:12:5: Secondly, because they are testimony of his fatherly good will toward us, insomuch that they show themselves to be bastards, which cannot abide to be chastened of God.
58:12:9: Thirdly, if all men yield this right to fathers, to whom next after God we owe this life, that they may rightfully correct their children, shall we not be much more subject to that our Father, who is the Author of the spiritual and everlasting life?
58:12:10: An amplification of the same argument: Those fathers have corrected us after their fancy, for some frail and transitory profit: but God chasteneth and instructeth us for our singular profit, to make us partakers of his holiness: which thing although these our senses do not presently perceive, yet the end of the matter proveth it.
58:12:12: The description of a man that is out of heart and clean discouraged.
The conclusion, we must go forward courageously and keep always a right course, and (as far forth as we may) without any staggering or stumbling.
58:12:13: Keep a right course, and so, that you show example of good life for others to follow.
58:12:14: We must live in peace, and holiness with all men.
58:12:15: That no heresy, or backsliding be an offense.
We must study to edify one another, both in doctrine and example of life.
58:12:16: We must eschew fornication, and a profane mind, that is, such a mind, as giveth not to God his due honor, which wickedness how severely God will at length punish, the horrible example of Esau teacheth us.
58:12:17: There was no place left for his repentance: and it appeareth by the effects, what his repentance was, for when he was gone out of his father’s sight, he threatened his brother to kill him.
58:12:18: Which might be touched with hands, which was of a gross and earthly matter.

Now he applieth the same exhortation, to the Prophetical and kingly office of Christ compared with Moses, after this sort, If the majesty of the Law was so great, how great think you that the glory of Christ and the Gospel is? And this comparison he declareth also particularly.
58:12:21: The shape and form which he saw, which was no counterfeit and forged shape, but a true one.
58:12:23: So he calleth them that are taken up into heaven, although one part of them sleep in the earth.
58:12:25: The applying of the former comparison, If it were not lawful to contemn his word which spake on the earth, how much less his voice which is from heaven?
58:12:26: It appeareth evidently in this that the Prophet speaketh of the calling of the Gentiles, that these words must be referred to the kingdom of Christ.

He compareth the steadfast majesty of the Gospel, wherewith the whole world was shaken, and even the very frame of heaven was as it were astonished, with the small and vanishing sound of the governance by the Law.
58:12:28: A general exhortation to live reverently and religiously under the most happy subjection of so mighty a king, who as he blesseth his most mightily, so doth he most severely revenge the rebellious. And this is the sum of a Christian life, respecting the first table.
By reverence is meant that honest shamefastness which keepeth them in their duties.
58:13:1: He cometh to the second table, the sum whereof is charity, especially toward strangers and such as are afflicted.
58:13:3: Be so much touched, as if their misery were yours.
58:13:4: He commendeth chaste matrimony in all sorts of men, and threateneth utter destruction from God, against whoremongers and adulterers.
58:13:5: Covetousness is condemned, against which is set a contented mind with that which the Lord hath given.
58:13:8: He repeateth the sum of the doctrine, to wit, the only ground of all precepts of manners, and that is this: That we ought to quiet and content ourselves in Christ only: for there was yet never any man saved without the knowledge of him, neither is at this day saved, neither shall be saved hereafter.
We have to set before us the examples of valiant Captains, whom we ought diligently to follow.
58:13:9: Which observed the difference of them superstitiously.
He toucheth them which mixed an external worship, and especially the difference of meats, with the Gospel, which doctrine he plainly condemneth as clean repugnant to the benefit of Christ.
By this one kind which concerneth the difference of clean and unclean meats, we have to understand all the ceremonial worship.
58:13:10: Whereof they cannot be partakers which stubbornly retain the rites of the Law.

He refuteth their error by an apt and fit comparison. They which in times past served the Tabernacle, did not eat of the sacrifices whose blood was brought for sin into the holy place by the high Priest. Moreover these sacrifices did represent Christ our offering. Therefore they cannot be partakers of him which serve the Tabernacle, that is, such as stand in the service of the Law: but let not us be ashamed to follow him out of Jerusalem, from whence he was cast out and suffered: for in this also Christ, who is the truth, answereth that figure, in that he suffered without the gate.
By the Altar, he meaneth the offering.
58:13:13: He goeth on further in this comparison, and showeth that this also signified unto us, that the godly followers of Christ must as it were go out of the world, bearing his cross.
58:13:15: Now that those corporal sacrifices are taken away, he teacheth us that the true sacrifices of confession remain, which consist partly in giving of thanks, and partly in liberality, with which sacrifices indeed God is now delighted.
58:13:17: We must obey the warnings and admonitions of our Ministers and Elders, which watch for the salvation of the souls which are committed unto them.
58:13:18: The last part of this Epistle, wherein he commendeth his ministry to the Hebrews, and wisheth them continuance and increase of graces from the Lord: and excuseth himself in that he hath used but few words to comfort them, having spent the Epistle in disputing: and saluteth certain brethren familiarly and friendly.
58:13:21: Hence cometh that saying of the Fathers, that God crowneth his works in us.
